citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
It was discovered two days ago that the licensee's population of dogs is infected with fleas. The licensee has begun
treatment of the population, but is not following the instructions in the program of veterinary care or contacted the
attending veterinarian to find out how to properly treat the population of dogs. Not following the program of veterinary care
or contacting the attending veterinarian doesn't ensure that the use of appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose,
and treat diseases, injuries, and problems is being used. The licensee must follow the program of veterinary care or
contact the attending veterinarian to ensure the population is being treated properly. Correct starting on 10/30/26.

Multiple outdoor enclosures had rust on the fencing and posts. Rust does not allow for the enclosure to be readily cleaned
and sanitized. All enclosures must be constructed and maintained so they are free of rust and can be readily cleaned and
sanitized. Correct by 11/29/26.

It was discovered two days ago that the licensee's population of dogs is infected with fleas. The licensee has begun
treatment of the population, but hasn't documented the problem or the plan for treatment and care. Not documenting the
problem or the plan for treatment and care doesn't allow for APHIS officials to ensure the population of dogs is being
treated properly by a plan laid out by the the Attending Veterinarian. All injuries/illnesses/problems to any dog or the
population as a whole must be documented going forward. All diagnoses/prognoses and treatment plans must also be
documented by the licensee as required under the Animal Welfare Act. Correct starting on 10/30/26.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
